ok its sunday night so im doing my planner for the week (washi tape and all) can u help me block it out pls

anatomy MWF 9am, gen chem TTh 11, stats is online. i work mon and wed noon to 6

Happy to help! Here's a first pass at your week, with a bit of explanation on each block so you can adjust.

Monday: You have anatomy at 9, and your shift starts at noon, so there's a natural window between class and work. I'd use 10:00-11:30 for a quick review of what was covered that morning while it's fresh, then lunch before you head in. After your shift, which ends at 6, you could do a light evening block for stats, maybe starting around 7:30 once you've eaten and had a breather.

Tuesday: Chem is at 11, which leaves the morning open. A focused anatomy session from 8 to 10 would work well, then a short pre-class review of chem notes around 10:15. In the afternoon you could do chem problem sets and stats modules, and since there's no work, you could spread these out with breaks.

Wednesday: This looks much like Monday, with anatomy at 9, review after, lunch, and work from noon to 6. Evening is a good time for flashcards or a lighter task.

Thursday: Chem at 11, so mornings are for anatomy reading or stats, and afternoon is a good time for chem homework.

Friday: Anatomy at 9, then the rest of the day can go to catching up and a weekly review so the weekend is lighter.

If you tell me about weekend commitments, I can add those too.

also one more thing. how do i not have the pharmacy convo w my mom this week. i told her im set on pharmacy and she keeps wanting to talk about it..

where would i even put that in the week

Here's one way to handle it:

- Don't schedule it this week. Early in the term you have a lot going on, and it's fine to wait.
- If she brings it up, a short deflection works: "I'm focused on anatomy right now, can we talk after my first practical?"
- Pick a rough date for the real conversation, like a weekend after your first big exam, and write it in your planner as a tentative block (say 30 minutes, after dinner).
- Before then, jot down in a few lines what you want to say, so it's ready.

Want me to draft that short deflection a few different ways?
